sections.content: Use the *pretérito* *perfecto* to talk about recent actions and experiences connected to the present. Review the auxiliary forms he, has, ha, hemos and *han* with past participles. Family members can be the subject of the sentence: Mi *madre* ha *llamado*. *Mis* *padres* han *hablado*.

items.spanish: Mi padre ha hablado con mi hermana.
items.english: My father has spoken with my sister.
My family has spoken with me.

sections.content: String the five auxiliary forms into one memorable chain: he, has, ha, *hemos*, *han* — the same five endings you would use for any -ar/-er/-ir verb in the present, just borrowed here for haber.
